_metadata.independence: Apart from the brief, I read only x15-ra-input.json; I opened no other file, searched nothing and used no web or API.

hints.reason: AIR via the Air Jordan nickname and Nike sneaker line, BASKETBALL via Michael Jordan himself; instant and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Easy but clean; strictly the 'Air Jordan' name began as Nike's shoe brand, but the explanation's framing is common and harmless.

hints.reason: Both sides come from the Snow White witch: her APPLE is laced with POISON; one scene supplies both words cleanly.

pairs.pair_note: Solid story clue; the queen-in-disguise detail is accurate to the Disney film.

hints.reason: Anatomical spine runs down your BACK; a BOOK's spine is its bound edge; a crisp double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Textbook double meaning, likely the best possible hint for this pair.

hints.reason: BANANA via the banana-crazy Despicable Me Minions, BOSS via the ordinary sense of a minion serving a boss (and the Minions serving Gru); fun aha.

pairs.pair_note: Pop-culture plus dictionary sense; the Minions' whole premise is serving a boss, which reinforces it.

hints.reason: BAR via the classic Boston-bar sitcom (and cheers said at any bar), TOAST via the word said when raising a glass.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; TOAST's bread sense is a nice decoy.

hints.reason: SINK via the sink drain, BASKETBALL via 'drain a shot' slang; the extra pun that sinking a shot also means draining it adds a real click.

pairs.pair_note: 'Drain a three' is well known to anyone who watches basketball; non-fans may need the explanation, but it lands.

hints.reason: BELT via the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter, DINOSAUR via the impact that ended the dinosaurs 66 million years ago; both facts are correct and widely known.

pairs.pair_note: Nice indirect-knowledge clue; BELT reading as clothing makes the aha better.

hints.reason: BITE via a nip being a small bite, FROST via 'Jack Frost nipping at your nose' from The Christmas Song; a lovely aha.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; 'frost-nip' is also a real term, adding a second route to FROST.

hints.reason: BOAT via tugboat, ROPE via tug-of-war (and tugging on a rope); both joins are instantly familiar and the pulling sense unifies them.

pairs.pair_note: A phrase-join that earns its pass because 'tug' also literally describes what you do to a rope.

hints.reason: BOX via the myth of Pandora's box, CHARM via the Pandora jewelry brand's charm bracelets; myth plus brand is a pleasing pairing.

pairs.pair_note: The brand side is very familiar to many U.S. players but less so to some; BOX side is universal, so it stays fair.

hints.reason: CAMERA via the camera shutter, WINDOW via window shutters; clean and accurate double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Clear, easy and correct.

hints.reason: CAP via Yankee Doodle's feather in his cap (and the iconic Yankees cap), NEW YORK via the New York Yankees; two independent routes both land.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; 'most famous team' is an opinion but a widely shared one.

hints.reason: CHAIR via Goldilocks breaking Baby Bear's chair, PLANET via the habitable 'Goldilocks zone'; exactly the indirect-knowledge aha the owner favours.

pairs.pair_note: Goldilocks zone is popular-science vocabulary most adults have met; facts are correct.

hints.reason: SHAPE via mold as a verb or form, CHEESE via the deliberate mold in blue cheese; accurate and satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Good double meaning; cheese is also pressed in molds, a bonus route.

hints.reason: CHURCH via the pipe organ, SKIN via the well-known fact that skin is the body's largest organ; a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: One of the best in the batch; the 'largest organ' fact is the standard textbook claim.

hints.reason: SAND via the sand trickling through it, CLOCK via the hourglass as a 'sand clock' timekeeper; very direct but clear and correct.
hints.fix: An hourglass is an old-fashioned sand clock that measures time with falling sand.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and flat but fair; the fix only softens 'tells time', since an hourglass times an interval rather than telling the hour.

hints.reason: COMIC via comic-strip panels, JUDGE via a panel of judges; both senses are common and correct.

pairs.pair_note: Clean double meaning; COMIC as 'comedian' is a nice misdirect.

hints.reason: COUNTRY via Dolly Parton, SHEEP via Dolly the cloned sheep; two famous Dollys, and the facts are right.

pairs.pair_note: Delightful; Dolly the sheep was in fact named after Dolly Parton, a fun extra the explanation could mention.

hints.reason: CRICKET via Jiminy Cricket, STRING via the puppet's 'I've Got No Strings'; both are core Disney Pinocchio knowledge.

pairs.pair_note: CRICKET's sport sense makes the aha nicer; facts are accurate.

hints.reason: DECK via shuffling cards, SONG via shuffle play on a playlist; universal and correct.

pairs.pair_note: Clear modern-plus-classic double use.

hints.reason: GENIUS via a brilliant mind, DIAMOND via the round brilliant cut and diamonds' brilliance; both senses honest.

pairs.pair_note: The cut name is moderately known, but 'brilliant' for a sparkling diamond is common enough that the DIAMOND side holds.

hints.reason: DOWN via goose down filling, DUCK via the game Duck, Duck, Goose; both instantly familiar and DOWN's directional sense hides the answer well.

pairs.pair_note: A phrase-join that is genuinely satisfying; ducks are also birds, adding a third thread.

hints.reason: GOLF via the birdie score, EAGLE via being both a bird and the golf score one better than a birdie; scoring facts are correct.

pairs.pair_note: Easy because EAGLE and GOLF already relate; still a clean, accurate clue.

hints.reason: SPOT via Dalmatians' spots (and Spot as a dog name), ENGINE via the firehouse-dog tradition on fire engines; classic Americana.

pairs.pair_note: Historically they ran beside horse-drawn engines, but riding on fire trucks as mascots is a fair modern image.

hints.reason: FAN via sports fans filling the stadium, WAVE via the stadium wave they do; one scene, both words, and both targets' other senses (electric fan, ocean wave) mislead nicely.

pairs.pair_note: Scene clue that clicks; fine as an easy one.

hints.reason: FILM via film reels, FISHING via the fishing reel; classic and accurate.

pairs.pair_note: Familiar double meaning; the 'reel/real' sound adds a little charm.

hints.reason: STATUE via the Statue of Liberty, FRANCE via its being France's gift to the U.S.; well-known and true.

pairs.pair_note: Straightforward history clue; liberty is also in France's national motto, a bonus thread.

hints.reason: GROUND via 'Ground Control' and MAJOR via 'Major Tom', both from Bowie's Space Oddity opening line; two odd-looking words click together at once.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent classic-rock clue. Note that MAJOR is also the hint for p_military__scale; avoid both on one board.

hints.reason: HEEL via stiletto heels, KNIFE via the stiletto dagger (whose shape named the heel); accurate and satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; HEEL's foot sense and wrestling sense both misdirect.

hints.reason: IRON via Tony Stark as Iron Man, WINTER via House Stark's words 'Winter Is Coming'; two huge franchises, one surname.

pairs.pair_note: Game of Thrones is not a PG show, but its motto is mainstream, inoffensive pop culture, so the clue is fine.

hints.reason: JUMP via vault as a leap (pole vault, gymnastics vault), SAFE via a bank vault; clean double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; SAFE's adjective sense hides the noun nicely.

hints.reason: MAGNET via its north and south poles, SANTA via his North Pole home; a pleasing, instantly fair aha.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent. SANTA appears in p_santa__tail too; board-level only.

hints.reason: MILITARY via the officer rank, SCALE via the major scale (do-re-mi); both senses accurate, and SCALE's weighing and fish senses misdirect.

pairs.pair_note: Good. MAJOR is a target in p_ground__major, so these two pairs must not share a board.

hints.reason: NAIL via a hammer driving nails, THUMB via the classic hammer-on-thumb mishap; a vivid, familiar scene.

pairs.pair_note: TACK (a small nail; thumbtack) is an alternative double, but HAMMER is equally good and funnier; both could pass.

hints.reason: PAINTING via the Mona Lisa and the Louvre's collection, PYRAMID via its glass pyramid entrance; PYRAMID pulling toward Egypt makes the aha land.

pairs.pair_note: Strong place-based clue; facts correct.

hints.reason: PINK via completing the band name Pink Floyd, WALL via their famous album The Wall; instantly familiar to a classic-rock-aware audience.

pairs.pair_note: PINK side is a phrase-join, WALL side a real album reference; passes because both are instantly familiar. Bonus: the album's main character is named Pink.

hints.reason: SOCK via sock puppet is instant, but PUNCH via the Punch and Judy show is a British seaside tradition that many U.S. players know only as a phrase, so that side may not click during play.

pairs.pair_note: Genuinely unsure: older U.S. players may know Punch and Judy as puppets. The pair also has an untapped route (PUNCH and SOCK both mean to hit), but no single-word hint for it beats PUPPET on delight.

hints.reason: SCREEN via a computer monitor, REPTILE via monitor lizards such as the Komodo dragon; accurate and a nice aha.

pairs.pair_note: Strong double meaning; monitor lizard is familiar enough for most adults.

hints.reason: SANTA via Comet the reindeer, TAIL via a comet's glowing tail; both are widely known and the facts are right.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent. Shares SANTA with p_magnet__santa; board-level only.

hints.reason: SKULL via Hamlet holding Yorick's skull, TOWN via a hamlet being a tiny village; Shakespeare plus dictionary, a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: One of the best in the batch.

hints.reason: SOLDIER via a captain leading soldiers (Captain America is one), WINTER only via the film title Captain America: The Winter Soldier; once WINTER and SOLDIER are spotted together, the title clicks.

pairs.pair_note: WINTER side leans on the film title, which also contains SOLDIER, so it is less elegant than a double meaning but still fair for a Marvel-aware audience. CAPTAIN contains CAP, a target in p_cap__new-york; keep those apart on a board.

hints.reason: SUIT via spades in a deck of cards, TOOL via the digging spade; clean and correct, and SUIT's clothing sense misdirects.

pairs.pair_note: Solid double meaning. TOOL also appears in p_tool__tooth; board-level only.

hints.reason: TOOL via the pick or pickaxe, TOOTH via toothpick (and the dentist's pick); familiar on both sides, though unremarkable.

pairs.pair_note: TOOL is a broad category, so PICK works mainly through the toothpick join; fair and clear but low on delight.
